cells.tense: The choice is already made and you're standing inside it — the two have run together long enough that it's less a decision now than the way you move.
cells.ask: Show the joined thing whole to one person who's only heard it described — say it end to end without stopping to fix it, and let their face tell you what's actually there.
cells.core:
What you're making comes out with your shape on it, and not because you've been sanding the seams off. The aim and the work move at the same speed, which is why the thing lands where people can see it and not only in your notes. If it starts to drift — the aim outrunning the work, or the work wandering somewhere the aim didn't ask for — the way back is the one already under your feet: let the direction come out of how engaged you actually are, not out of a plan sketched once and defended since.

Something like this gets tested against somebody soon. Carry it out of what you feel pulled toward, not out of what you settled on about it earlier.

cells.tense: You're bracing for a version of this that hasn't arrived — rehearsing the merge, guarding the merge, fixing a problem that's still weeks off.
cells.ask: Pick the piece you've tended longest and leave it untouched for a day — no checking, no adjusting. Whatever still stands when you come back is the part that holds.
cells.core:
You're gripping the joined thing to keep it from coming apart, and the grip has started causing the exact thing you were guarding against. Conversations turn into proof, work turns into defense, and the easy part — two things flowing because they want to — gets harder to find. There's a difference between a hand that holds and a hand that clutches, and you can feel it in yours. What made this good at the start was holding it lightly.

What got built here got built by care, and care doesn't have to run all night to count. Set it down for one day and let it stand without you. You'll find out what's growing and what you were propping up — either answer is worth having in your hands.

cells.tense: A choice got made back there and you've been at the door since — the two have already met, and the part of you that would walk through is still at the threshold.
cells.ask: Tell one person the plain sentence about where this is going — no caveats, no warm-up, just the line you've been keeping in your pocket.
cells.core:
Done well, the picture arrives and the next move happens in the same breath — the call gets made while the thing is still warm. Yours arrives and then sits. A reply gets hedged, a call gets held, more information gets waited on and it isn't coming, and from the outside the waiting passes for careful.

What's asked is smaller than certainty: put one sentence into the air, out loud, and see what it does. Acting on what lands, instead of on what you can defend in advance, is the whole of it. You don't have to be sure. You just have to stop requiring sure before you open your mouth.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you're already writing — you're shaping this thing and calling it what the work does rather than what you're doing.
cells.ask: Take one piece of this you've been calling what the moment needed and say your name next to it, out loud, once.
cells.core:
You talk about this in the passive voice — it came together, it's working, it's what the situation asked for. But no situation here is making the calls. The shaping comes from you, quietly, each time you pick the thing that fits over the thing that's easy, and a person close to this would notice if you stopped.

Come back to the plain version: take the same eye you use to see what fits and turn it on one decision you've been calling obvious. It isn't obvious. It's you meeting the moment and dressing it up as the moment's own logic. Underneath, the hand on the tiller is yours.
